title: Visual reference catalog

story.actor: designer, developer, content author, or connected product collaborator
story.need: inspect the real appearance and responsive behavior of governed screens, flows, patterns, and content blocks
story.outcome: new work can select and reuse a proven visual pattern without reconstructing it from prose

scope: Replace the text-card reference route with a visual catalog workbench
Render every supported content-block family with representative content
Expose every governed visual variant through a live variant selector
Provide desktop, tablet, and mobile preview widths
Represent screens, flows, and interaction patterns with meaningful visual specimens
Keep stable reference IDs and implementation notes available as secondary details
Support searching and keyboard-accessible category and specimen selection
nonGoals: Copying licensed Tailwind Plus example source into the product or documentation
Editing production content from the catalog
Replacing the public-site renderer with a second catalog-only renderer
Treating visual examples as approval to bypass feature specifications
dataRequirements: Catalog selection, search, variant, and viewport are ephemeral browser state
Block specimens use deterministic representative fixtures and never query site content
Stable catalog IDs remain identical to their feature-spec and MCP identifiers
Licensed source filenames and package contents are never exposed at runtime
permissions: Catalog previews cannot invoke content mutations
Public catalog visibility does not expose administrative or licensed source data

acceptanceCriteria.given: a visitor opens the reference catalog
then: all seventeen block families are selectable
the selected block is rendered with representative content using the production renderer
every governed variant for that block can be selected and seen
the preview can be constrained to desktop, tablet, or mobile width

acceptanceCriteria.given: a visitor browses screens, flows, or patterns
then: the primary artifact is a visual specimen or diagram rather than a prose card
the stable ID and concise usage guidance remain visible beside the specimen

acceptanceCriteria.given: a visitor uses a keyboard or narrow viewport
acceptanceCriteria.when: they search, change category, select a specimen, or change preview controls
then: every control has an accessible name and visible focus state
selection state is conveyed without relying on color alone
the catalog remains usable without horizontal page overflow
the existing 179-entry coverage contract still passes
no licensed source package is included in Git or a container build context

fixtures: representative deterministic content for all seventeen block families
a block family with one variant and a family with twelve or more variants
screen miniatures for list, create, editor, history, media, and settings
flow diagrams for draft/publish, MCP operation, and environment promotion
desktop, tablet, and mobile preview widths
verification: Reference catalog browser contracts on desktop and mobile
Accessibility scan of the visual workbench
Reference, Marketing coverage, build, UAT, and production verification loops
